name: Capture Timeline
why: Each government site was hit by bursts of Arquivo.pt "save a web page" captures, from a few dozen (Justice, 40) to hundreds of thousands (Maryland, 295,945; Education, 219,923). The CSVs hide the shape: when each burst started, how fast it ran (up to about 5,600 captures a minute), when the site began answering with errors (Kansas turned to 504 timeouts for most of its 36,579 captures), and how the requested URLs changed step by step (State_Id=0, -1, 99, 999, then "1 OR 1=1"). A lane per site with status-coloured volume, plus an ordered log of the URLs in any time range, lets the analyst see each site's story and the moment the requests turned from normal to probing.
arrangement:
Unit: One capture: one row of a section's arquivo-captures.csv, keyed by section folder + record_number. 561,326 rows across 12 sections (01-education 219,923; 02-canada 899; 03-kansas 36,579; 04-illinois 251; 05-maryland 295,945; 06-new-york 715; 08-california 111; 09-max-gov 26; 10-navy 3,729; 11-justice 40; 12-bea 3,011). Fields: captured_at_utc, target_url, indexed_http_status, reviewed_origin_status (Illinois only), mime, collection, source_url_redacted, archive_url.
Overview: One horizontal lane per section (named by site, e.g. "Kansas – kansasmemory.gov"), each with its own time axis fitted to that section's active period (most sections are one day; Maryland has 21 captures on 2026-03-02 and the rest on 2026-05-06; Navy has April 23-24 and May 18), since the sections span March to June 2026 and a shared axis would squash them. In each lane, a bar per minute of captures, stacked by status class (2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx, 5xx), with the lane's total, peak captures per minute and share of 2xx written beside it. Pre-aggregate per minute in the backend: two files exceed 200k rows.
Zoom: Brush a time range in a lane to open its capture log below: captures in time order with time, status, mime and target_url. Collapse runs of captures whose URLs differ only in a cache-busting parameter (zz=..., uniq=..., x=...) or a single incrementing number into one row "×N" with the range of values. Highlight in each URL the part that changed from the previous distinct URL, so a sequence like State_Id=0 → -1 → 99 → 999 → 1 OR 1=1 reads at a glance. URL-decode for display but keep the raw URL on hover.
Filter: Filter by section, status class, mime, host (some sections use raw IPs, user@host tricks or trailing dots, e.g. Illinois 216.124.54.114), a substring or regex on target_url, and source_url_redacted. Labels that are on mark captures in the log and colour the bars; the Labels pane's filter limits both. Two sections can be shown side by side for comparison.
Details: Clicking a capture shows every column of its row, the archive_url as a link to Arquivo.pt's replay, and, when sources.csv in the same section names a responses/*.txt file for that URL, the text of that response body.
